title: No Man's Sky: starship controls on stick and throttle

sources.title: No Man's Sky controls (Carl's Guides, PC / PlayStation / Xbox defaults)

intro: No Man's Sky (Hello Games) is an exploration game where the player flies a starship between planets and stars. All ship types share the same controls: the cockpit has the flight data on the canopy glass, and most ship jobs are done in menus. The game has no ready-made stick and throttle layout; this guide explains the game's own ship actions in the places JoyPro suggests for them.

areas.name: Canopy HUD
areas.text: The flight data on the cockpit glass.

panels.name: Cockpit HUD (canopy and dashboard)
panels.text: The HUD shows the flight data on the cockpit glass and the dashboard: speed, shield and hull, the weapon, the fuel and markers for places and targets.
panels.context: It looks the same in every ship type; the pilot reads it while flying, fighting or looking for a place to land.

controls.name: Speed
controls.text: This shows how fast the ship is flying. While the pulse engine is on, it shows the much higher pulse speed.
controls.context: The throttle sets the normal speed; the pulse button on the throttle switches to pulse flight for long distances inside a star system.

controls.name: Shield and hull
controls.text: This shows the starship's shield, a protective layer that takes hits first, and the hull, the ship's body.
controls.context: When the shield is empty, hits damage the hull; the shield is recharged from the quick menu.

controls.name: Weapon and heat
controls.text: This shows which ship weapon is selected and how hot it is. A weapon that gets too hot has to cool down before it fires again.
controls.context: The thumb button on the stick changes the weapon; firing in short bursts keeps the heat down.

controls.name: Fuel
controls.text: This shows the fuel for the launch thrusters (needed to take off from the ground) and for the pulse engine.
controls.context: Without launch fuel the ship cannot take off; the pilot refuels the technology from the quick menu.

controls.name: Markers
controls.text: Marks on the view show targets, bases, space stations and things found by the scanner.
controls.context: The scan button on the stick adds new markers for nearby places.

areas.name: Dashboard and menus
areas.text: The menus for recharging, inventory and the galactic map.

panels.name: Quick menu and inventory
panels.text: These are menus over the view for ship jobs that have no own button: recharging equipment, calling the big freighter, calling a ground vehicle, the ship's inventory and the galactic map.
panels.context: The hat on the stick opens the quick menu and the galactic map in this layout.

controls.name: Quick menu
controls.text: The quick menu recharges the ship's technology (for example the shield or the fuel), calls the player's freighter and summons exocraft, the ground vehicles.
controls.context: It opens with the hat pushed up; the pilot uses it often during long trips.

controls.name: Ship inventory
controls.text: The inventory shows the ship's cargo and the technology slots where equipment is installed.
controls.context: Each ship type has a different number of slots; better classes have more.

controls.name: Galactic map
controls.text: The galactic map shows other star systems that the hyperdrive, the drive for jumps between stars, can reach.
controls.context: The pilot picks the next star here and then jumps from space; it opens with the hat pushed down.

areas.name: Stick and throttle
areas.text: The stick steers and fights; the throttle sets the speed, boost and the pulse engine.

panels.name: Stick
panels.text: The stick steers the ship and holds the buttons for the weapon, the scanner, landing and the menus.
panels.context: No Man's Sky has no ready-made layout for a stick and throttle. The actions are the game's own; where they sit on the stick is JoyPro's suggestion, set up with Steam Input or the game's own key settings.

controls.name: Stick (pitch, turn, roll)
controls.text: Pushing the stick forward or pulling it back tips the nose down or up. Left and right turn the ship (yaw), and twisting the stick rolls it.
controls.context: In this suggestion left and right turn instead of rolling, which makes aiming at targets easier.

controls.name: Trigger (fire)
controls.text: Pulling the trigger fires the selected ship weapon.
controls.context: It shoots at pirates, Sentinels and rocks; the HUD shows the weapon's heat.

controls.name: Thumb button (weapon mode)
controls.text: This button changes to the next ship weapon that is installed.
controls.context: Different weapons suit shooting ships or breaking asteroids; the HUD shows which one is active.

controls.name: Head button left (scan)
controls.text: This button uses the ship's scanner, which finds interesting places nearby and marks them.
controls.context: New markers then appear on the HUD; the scanner needs a moment before the next scan.

controls.name: Head button right (land / exit)
controls.text: Near the ground this button lands the ship. Once landed, pressing it again lets the pilot climb out.
controls.context: The game lands the ship by itself when the pilot presses it close to a flat place or a landing pad.

controls.name: Hat (menus)
controls.text: Pushing the hat up opens the quick menu; pushing it down opens the galactic map.
controls.context: Both menus handle ship jobs that have no own button, such as recharging or picking the next star.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: The throttle sets the speed and holds the buttons for boost and the pulse engine.
panels.context: As with the stick, these places are JoyPro's suggestion for the game's own actions.

controls.name: Throttle lever (speed up / slow down)
controls.text: Pushing the lever forward makes the ship faster; pulling it back slows it down.
controls.context: Flying slower makes landing and aiming easier; the HUD shows the speed.

controls.name: Thumb button (boost)
controls.text: Holding this button gives a burst of extra speed.
controls.context: Boost helps to escape a fight or to cross a planet quickly; it is not the same as the pulse engine.

controls.name: Pulse button (pulse engine)
controls.text: This button switches on the pulse engine, a very fast drive for travelling between planets inside one star system.
controls.context: The pulse engine works in space only and uses its own fuel; the speed readout shows the pulse speed.
